thread:
maya: starting mango13b int4 canary 09:03. initial loads OK but seeing fragmentation and one OOM on canary-1 when a client sent a 1500 token request.
aj: saw that too. logs show KV allocation spikes after prefetch completes. prefetched shards ~1.6G, free mem ~200M then OOM on large gen.
toni: OOM snippet: ```OOM: allocate 1.2G failed
kv_slots_used=84/128
slab_frag=0.34
current_batch=2
max_new_tokens=1500```
liam: we onboarded with prefetch=1 and batch_autoprefetch enabled to speed up token time. seems int4 codepath increases transient allocations and doesn't compact well, leaving holes.
maya: proposed quick fixes: 1) lower default max_new_tokens to 512, 2) disable prefetch for mango13b-int4, 3) set default microbatch to 1, 4) enable kv_trim_on_eviction. also add a 2-request warmup after model load to stabilize allocator order.
aj: runbook note: customers with long-tail large generations should use a dedicated profile with reserved capacity or larger mem slot sizes. but defaults must be safe.
liam: I'll roll canary-2 with the new defaults and add a small churn compaction step after 5 minutes idle. pushing now.
ops-bot: deploy started: canary-2 mango13b-int4 by liam at 2026-03-21T16:10:00Z
maya: also scheduling a focused eval: 200 short prompts + 20 prompts >1000 tokens to catch quality/regressions after reducing max_new_tokens. will report diffs.
aj: if we still see OOMs we can try: kernel-level deferred allocation flag, and a background compactor that runs between requests when GPU load < 10%.
liam: metrics will stream to the model dashboard; I'll tag team with `#eng-ml` updates every 30m. ping if you want access to canary logs.
maya: thanks all — creating PR with defaults + metadata note about int4 frag and suggested profile for high-gen customers. reconvene in 1h.
